channel.title: Cipi guides
channel.description: Practical guides for Laravel and PHP on your own server.

item.title: Push to deploy or CI pipeline? Agent vs pipeline deploys for Laravel
item.description: How Cipi's two deploy modes work, side by side, with an honest verdict on when to use the agent's push-to-deploy webhook, when to use a CI pipeline, and how to switch between them.

item.title: Anonymize a Laravel database with Cipi Agent, step by step
item.description: Give developers, QA, staging and AI assistants a realistic copy of production with every personal field replaced, explained from zero: install the agent, scan the schema, review the rules, request a dump from your laptop, import it, and keep it GDPR-safe.

item.title: Back up Laravel apps and databases to S3, and restore them
item.description: Encrypted, scheduled backups of every app and database to AWS S3 or any S3-compatible storage (Hetzner, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO), with retention, verification and a tested restore.

item.title: Monitor Laravel errors and uptime with Boogle, self-hosted
item.description: Run Boogle, a free open-source exception tracker and uptime monitor, as a Cipi app, connect your Laravel apps to it, get e-mail alerts when something breaks or goes offline, and triage issues like a team, step by step from zero.

item.title: Add Laravel security checks (SAST) to CI with Checkpoint
item.description: Install Checkpoint, a free Laravel security scanner, run its 33 checks locally, read PASS, WARN and FAIL results, accept known findings, and block risky code in GitHub Actions or GitLab CI before Cipi deploys it, step by step.

item.title: Monitor a Laravel app's health with the Cipi Agent and any uptime service
item.description: Expose a token-protected health endpoint covering database, cache, queue, storage and the last deploy, and plug it into UptimeRobot, Better Stack, Grafana or a cron.

item.title: Cipi Agent: connect your Laravel app to its server
item.description: Install cipi/agent to get push-to-deploy, a health endpoint, an MCP server for AI assistants, cipi.yml validation and GDPR-safe database dumps in any Laravel app.

item.title: Push-to-deploy Laravel from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Gitea
item.description: Deploy on every git push with signed webhooks verified inside your app, branch filtering, an audit trail of who pushed, and deploys that never run inside a web request.

item.title: Install Cipi on AWS EC2
item.description: Launch an AWS EC2 instance for Laravel step by step (Ubuntu AMI, instance type, gp3 storage, security group, Elastic IP), install Cipi, point DNS, and connect S3, SES and CodeCommit.

item.title: Install Cipi on Amazon Lightsail
item.description: Create an AWS Lightsail instance for Laravel step by step (OS-only Ubuntu blueprint, plan, static IP, IPv4 and IPv6 firewall), install Cipi, point DNS and know when to move to EC2.

item.title: Install Cipi on a DigitalOcean Droplet
item.description: Create a DigitalOcean Droplet for Laravel step by step (image, size, SSH key, cloud firewall, reserved IP), install Cipi, point DNS, and use Spaces for off-site backups.

item.title: The Cipi web panel and REST API
item.description: Add an optional, self-hosted web panel for your team and clients, a REST API for automation, a CLI client for your laptop, and roles, 2FA and SSO, without giving up the terminal.

item.title: Install Cipi on Hetzner Cloud
item.description: Create a Hetzner Cloud server step by step (location, Ubuntu image, server type, SSH key, firewall, IPv4), install Cipi, point DNS and set up off-site backups to Hetzner Object Storage.

item.title: Manage Laravel in production with Claude, Cursor and the Cipi MCP
item.description: Connect Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code to your live Laravel app and to your server through Cipi's two MCP servers, with tokens, guardrails, secret redaction and an audit trail.

item.title: Cipi on Vultr, Akamai Linode, OVHcloud and Scaleway
item.description: Install Cipi on Vultr, Akamai Linode, OVHcloud, Scaleway or any provider: what to choose, provider by provider, a checklist for unknown providers, and fixes for the usual first-day problems.

item.title: cipi.yml recipes for common Laravel setups
item.description: 18 copy-paste cipi.yml recipes, each with when to use it and what to change: a first app, SaaS with Horizon and Reverb, Octane API, online shop, multi-tenant, staging, redirects, Next.js, Nuxt, static sites, long jobs, AI apps, backups and tuning.

item.title: Staging and production from one repository with cipi.yml
item.description: A beginner-friendly walkthrough to run a staging copy and a production copy of the same Laravel app, each deploying its own branch with its own settings, driven by cipi-staging.yml and cipi.yml.

item.title: Cloudflare in front of Laravel, explained: DNS, proxy, SSL modes and wildcards
item.description: Put a Laravel app on Cipi behind Cloudflare without redirect loops or broken certificates: DNS records, orange vs grey cloud, every SSL/TLS mode explained, wildcard certificates over DNS, real visitor IPs, caching rules, WAF, WebSockets and upload limits, step by step.

item.title: Put a Laravel server behind Cloudflare Zero Trust, step by step
item.description: From zero to a server with no open ports: what a Cloudflare Tunnel and Access are, the token and account you need, routing apps through the tunnel, a login wall for staging and the panel, SSH through Cloudflare, certificates that still renew, closing ports safely, and how to undo every step.

item.title: Block attackers automatically with CrowdSec on a Laravel server
item.description: What CrowdSec is and how it differs from Fail2ban and a WAF, enabling it safely on a Cipi server, the allowlists that keep you, your CDN and your Git provider from being banned, checking what it blocks, the break-glass rescue if you lock yourself out, and how to remove it.

item.title: Deploy Laravel on an Ubuntu VPS with zero downtime
item.description: From a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 server to a Laravel app on HTTPS with queues, scheduler and push-to-deploy, explained from zero: install, create the app, connect Git, deploy, HTTPS, rollbacks and the first-day problems.

item.title: Deploy a Symfony app on an Ubuntu VPS with Cipi
item.description: Host Symfony as a custom app with the public/ document root, Composer and cache warm-up after each deploy, a database, Messenger workers via cron, HTTPS and backups.

item.title: Host WordPress on your own VPS next to Laravel apps
item.description: Run WordPress as an isolated custom app with its own PHP pool, database, HTTPS, backups and Git or SFTP deploys, on the same server as your Laravel apps.

item.title: Security-test your Laravel apps with Hackly, self-hosted
item.description: Install Hackly, a free open-source security scanning platform, as a Cipi app on its own server, prove you own a domain, run DAST scans of your sites and SAST/SCA scans of your repositories, triage findings and export reports, step by step from zero.

item.title: Free, privacy-friendly website analytics with IndieStats
item.description: Replace Google Analytics with IndieStats, a free self-hosted analytics app without cookies or third parties: install it as a Cipi app, add the snippet to your sites, track events and goals, and configure retention and privacy for GDPR, step by step.

item.title: Your own S3 storage for Laravel with Johnny
item.description: Set up Johnny, free self-hosted S3-compatible object storage, on its own VPS, create buckets and scoped access keys, connect Laravel's filesystem, send Cipi backups to it, and import buckets from AWS, Spaces or R2, step by step from zero.

item.title: A Laravel API with a Next.js or Nuxt front end on one server
item.description: Run a Laravel API and a server-rendered Next.js or Nuxt front end side by side, each with its own domain, zero-downtime deploys and HTTPS, plus Sanctum for authentication.

item.title: Deploy Laravel with AWS CodeDeploy and Cipi
item.description: Let AWS CodeDeploy orchestrate releases while Cipi does the zero-downtime deploy on each server, on EC2 or outside AWS, with a health check, a correct rollback and GitHub Actions on top.

item.title: CI/CD for Laravel with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI
item.description: Test on every push and deploy only when tests pass, with a health check that rolls back a broken release, a dedicated CI key, an optional backup step and zero-downtime releases.

item.title: The self-hosted Laravel developer stack (2026)
item.description: Which parts of a Laravel team's toolchain are worth owning (servers, deploys, backups, search, analytics, error tracking) and which are still better bought, with the cost math.

item.title: The Laravel ecosystem in 2026, mapped to production
item.description: Octane, Horizon, Reverb, Scout, Pulse, Livewire, Filament, Inertia, Pest and the rest, grouped by the job they do, with what each one needs from your server.

item.title: Laravel .env and secrets in production, done right
item.description: What the .env file is, why it never goes in Git, where Cipi keeps it so it survives deploys and rollbacks, how to change values safely from the CLI, the panel or the API, rotating database passwords and API keys, config caching, and keeping secrets out of logs and AI tools.

item.title: Laravel queues and Horizon in production
item.description: Queues explained from zero, then everything for production on your own server: what a worker is, adding and scaling queues under Supervisor, timeouts and retries, switching to Horizon on Valkey, protecting the dashboard, deploys that never run old code, failed jobs, alerts and cipi.yml.

item.title: Deploy Laravel from Jenkins to your own server
item.description: A Jenkinsfile that runs your Laravel tests, deploys with Cipi over SSH or the API, checks the release and rolls back only when it should, plus approvals and a one-click rollback job.

item.title: Multi-tenant Laravel SaaS with wildcard subdomains
item.description: Build a SaaS where every customer gets their own subdomain, explained from zero: how wildcard DNS, routing and certificates fit together, setting them up with Cloudflare and Cipi, resolving the tenant in Laravel, custom domains for customers, and when to give a tenant its own app instead.

item.title: Laravel Octane with FrankenPHP on your own server
item.description: Serve Laravel from memory with Octane and FrankenPHP, side by side with PHP-FPM apps, with pinned builds, safe upgrades and zero-downtime reloads.

item.title: Laravel on PostgreSQL, on your own server
item.description: From zero to a Laravel app on PostgreSQL with Cipi: what Postgres is good at, installing it next to MariaDB, creating apps and extra databases on it, connecting from your laptop, backups, restores, upgrades and moving an existing app from MySQL.

item.title: Preview environments for every Laravel pull request
item.description: Give every pull request its own live URL with a database, workers and HTTPS, created when it opens, updated on every push and deleted when it closes, with one script and GitHub Actions or GitLab review apps.

item.title: Real-time Laravel with Reverb, on your own domain
item.description: Run Laravel Reverb WebSockets behind your app's own domain and certificate, with Supervisor, Nginx and Echo configured for you. No extra ports, no Pusher bill.

item.title: Laravel scheduler and cron jobs in production
item.description: How Laravel's task scheduler works on a server, explained from zero: the one cron line, how Cipi runs it per app, writing scheduled tasks that don't overlap, running them on one server only, extra cron jobs, alerts when a job fails and how to debug one that never ran.

item.title: Laravel Scout with Meilisearch, self-hosted
item.description: Add fast, typo-tolerant search to a Laravel app with Scout and a Meilisearch instance on your own server, isolated per app, with no Algolia bill.

item.title: Laravel production security checklist
item.description: A practical checklist for a Laravel app on your own server, covering the app, the PHP and nginx stack, access, data and monitoring, with the command that covers each item.

item.title: Laravel cache, sessions and queues on Valkey (Redis)
item.description: What Redis and Valkey are, when to move Laravel's cache, sessions and queues off the database, and how to do it on Cipi with one isolated Valkey instance per app: switching drivers, memory limits, eviction, moving off a shared instance, and debugging.

item.title: Zero-downtime Laravel deploys with safe migrations
item.description: How atomic releases work, how to write migrations that never break the live release, and how to take a database snapshot and roll back automatically when something goes wrong.

item.title: cipi.yml: keep your server settings in the repository
item.description: Keep PHP, workers, scheduler, domains, databases, health checks, backups and deploy options in a cipi.yml next to your Laravel code, explained from zero: generate it, edit it, validate it, review it in pull requests, plan and apply it safely.

item.title: Move a Laravel app from Forge (or Ploi) to Cipi
item.description: A step-by-step migration from Laravel Forge or Ploi to a free, open-source Cipi server: mapping each Forge feature to its Cipi equivalent, a fresh server, the app, the .env, the database, files, workers and scheduler, a DNS switch with almost no downtime, and a rollback plan.

item.title: Move Laravel apps to a new server with cipi sync
item.description: Migrate one app or a whole server between providers (AWS to Hetzner, an old VPS to a bigger one) with encrypted archives, the same deploy keys, database and storage, and a DNS switch when you're ready.

item.title: Server notifications: Telegram, Slack, e-mail and webhooks done right
item.description: Set up Cipi notifications from scratch, explained for beginners: which channels exist, which events trigger them, how to route urgent alerts to your phone and the rest to a quiet channel, how to verify signed webhooks, and how to avoid alert fatigue.

item.title: Self-host PHP e-commerce on a VPS: Bagisto, Lunar, Sylius, PrestaShop and more
item.description: A practical map of open-source PHP shop platforms and how to run each on your own server with Cipi, explained for beginners, with full setups for a Laravel-based shop (Bagisto) and a Symfony-based one (Sylius), plus what every shop needs.

item.title: How Cipi handled the November 2026 PHP and nginx CVEs
item.description: A real case study of the nginx 1.31.9 and PHP 8.x security releases of November 2026: which CVEs reached a Cipi server, which were closed by default settings, and how servers were patched without downtime.

item.title: Upgrade PHP for a Laravel app without downtime
item.description: How PHP versions work on a server, explained from zero: running several versions side by side, checking your code and Composer dependencies, moving one app at a time with zero downtime, rolling back, nightly security patches, end-of-life versions and Octane's own PHP.

item.title: What preview environments can do for your team
item.description: Why a live URL for every pull request changes how Laravel teams review, test, demo and ship, with ten concrete uses, an end-to-end testing recipe and the rules that keep previews cheap and safe on your own servers.

item.title: Server monitoring and alerts on Telegram, Slack and e-mail
item.description: Watch CPU, memory, disk, services, certificates and app health on your own server, and get alerted on Telegram, Slack, e-mail or a webhook when something actually breaks.

item.title: Spec-driven development with AI agents in Laravel
item.description: Write the spec first, let an agent implement it against tests, and close the loop on production through MCP, with guardrails that keep data and deploys safe.

item.title: VPS, SSH and DNS for Laravel developers who never ran a server
item.description: The words and the three skills you need before deploying to your own server, explained from zero: what a VPS is, choosing one, creating an SSH key, logging in, pointing a domain with DNS records, checking it worked, and what Cipi takes care of so you don't have to.

item.title: WooCommerce on your own VPS, step by step
item.description: Host a WooCommerce shop on an Ubuntu VPS from zero, explained for beginners: an isolated app, the database, HTTPS, PHP limits for a shop, real cron for Action Scheduler, caching, frequent backups, a staging copy and security.
